tool_input.command: cat src/theme.rs && sed -n 1,80p src/delete.rs && which gio && gio version; git status --short
tool_input.description: Read theme, delete header, check gio
Patch ui.rs with collector state and handlers
Print headless renders from the render test

result:
The trash collector is implemented in the files I own, and `cargo check` and `cargo test` pass with 39 tests. It has not been run against a real desktop Trash or in a real terminal: the tests use a fake executor, and I eyeballed renders through the test backend only.

Some Bash calls were denied by the permission mode: compound and piped commands, and a Python patch script. I did not work around those denials. I used Read/Write/Edit instead and ran only plain `cargo` and `rustfmt` commands.

## Files
- **New:** `src/collector.rs`, `src/trash.rs`, `src/ui/review.rs`
- **Edited:** `src/main.rs`, `src/ui.rs`, `src/ui/view.rs`
- No changes to `Cargo.toml`, the lock file, `scan.rs`, `delete.rs`, `theme.rs`, docs, or scripts. No new dependencies.

## Controls
- **Browse:**
  - `Space` collects or uncollects the highlighted entry.
  - `c` opens the review.
  - `d` plus typing `delete` is unchanged and still permanent. Its flow was edited only to carry the collector across the post-delete rescan.
- **Review:**
  - `↑↓` or `jk` move through rows.
  - `Space` or `Backspace` removes the selected row.
  - `t` opens the Trash confirmation. On an empty collector it shows an explicit message instead.
  - `Esc` closes the review.
- **Confirm:** type `trash` then `Enter`; `Esc` returns to the review. Typing `delete` never starts the batch.
- **During the batch:** `Esc` stops after the current item finishes.
- The header always shows the count and allocated total, or `◇ collector empty`.
- Markers appear in both the list and the map tiles: `◆` collected, `◇` inside a collected folder, `!` stale or failed.
- The review shows a row per item with size, kind and tail-truncated path; per-item error lines; and the full wrapped path and status for the selected row. It also shows the total, the controls, an empty state, and the note "Space is freed when Trash is emptied, not now."

## APIs useful to independent tests
- **Collector:**
  - `collector::Collector::new(trash::Guard)` builds a collector.
  - `toggle(&root, &route, index)` returns `Toggle::{Added{replaced}, Removed, Covered(parent), Refused(why)}`.
  - Other methods: `reconcile(&root)`, `apply(&Report)`, `records()`, `mark(path)`, `total_bytes()`, `attention()`, `remove(i)`.
- **Record fields:** raw `path`, `identity` (device+inode), `kind`, `bytes`, `files`, `root`, `chain` (root and ancestor identities), `stale`, `error`. No route indices or tree clones are kept.
- **Trash:**
  - `trash::preflight(&Record, &Guard)` runs the pre-move checks.
  - `trash::run_batch(records, guard, &dyn Executor, &cancel, &done)` returns a `Report` with `outcomes`, `attempted`, `cancelled` and `summary()`.
  - `trash::Executor` is the trait seam for injecting a fake executor.
  - `trash::gio_command(path)` builds exactly `gio trash -- ABS`, refuses relative paths, and uses no shell.
  - `Guard { trash_dirs, mounts }` with `Guard::from_system()`.
- **App:**
  - `ui::App::with_collector` builds an App with an injected collector.
  - `App::rebuild(root, secs)` preserves the collector and the current location. It is used after a manual rescan, a permanent delete and a batch trash.
  - Also available: `toggle_collect`, `open_review`, and `review_key(KeyCode) -> bool` (true means run the batch).
- **Snapshots:** `--snapshot collector`, `collector-browse`, `collector-confirm`, `collector-errors` and `collector-empty`. The errors state applies a fabricated report and executes nothing.

## Checks run
- `cargo check` is clean, with no warnings.
- `rustfmt` was applied to owned files only. A `--check` run confirmed no unowned file would change.
- `cargo test` covers the following, using a fake executor that moves items to a private temp directory:
  - Parent/child normalisation and totals.
  - The ancestor chain recorded for each item.
  - The original identity is kept across a rescan and an App rebuild; after a remove the item can be recollected.
  - A vanished item or a replaced parent is marked stale.
  - Refusals: replaced target, changed type, symlinked or replaced ancestor, replaced or symlinked scan root.
  - Rejections: the root itself, paths outside it, `..`, and relative paths.
  - Trash protection for the home Trash, volume `.Trash`/`.Trash-uid` directories, mount points, and ancestors that contain a Trash.
  - A partial batch where a refused item never reaches the executor and failed files stay intact.
  - Cancellation between items.
  - gio reports success but the item is still there.
  - gio argument boundaries for `-rf`, shell metacharacters, newlines, non-UTF-8 names and `--`.
  - Review keys and the typed confirmation.
  - Renders at 60×20, 80×24, 140×44 and 300×90.

## Limitations
- **Not atomic.** Preflight verifies the root, each ancestor and the target by device+inode, but `gio` then re-resolves the absolute path. A concurrent writer can swap a path in that window, so this is best-effort only. A gio success where the collected inode is still at the path is reported as failed.
- **Volume Trash detection:**
  - Collect time: any scanned subdirectory named `.Trash` or `.Trash-<digits>` anywhere in the subtree refuses the collect. This is conservative.
  - Preflight: only direct `.Trash`/`.Trash-<euid>` children are re-checked, plus the mount-point list read at App creation. A volume mounted later is not seen.
- **Staleness model:**
  - `stale` is advisory and recomputed on each rescan; the live preflight is what actually decides whether an item is refused.
  - `error` from a batch persists until the item is removed.
  - Collected totals are scan-time allocated bytes; items the scan counted as shared hard links show as 0.
- **Rescans.**
  - When every item was refused, gio never ran, so there is no rescan.
  - When a rescan does run, quitting the rescan-failure screen exits the program and prints the summary; the collector is in-session only and is lost there.
- **Failures:**
  - A terminal I/O error mid-batch joins the worker and then exits with the summary, the same as the delete flow.
  - A gio failure surfaces the first stderr line.
  - Nothing falls back to deletion, and no message claims space was freed.
- **Wireframe mode** has the same keys but draws neither the markers nor the review, so the collector cannot be seen or reviewed there.

Missing: nothing from the brief that I am aware of. README, docs and acceptance scripts are untouched, as they belong to root.
